dataset: RFW test set (Wang et al., ICCV 2019), four subsets Caucasian / Asian / Indian / African, loosely cropped 400x400 .jpg, all identities (every identity has >= 2 images)
dataset_limitations: RFW group labels are the subset an identity was placed in by the dataset authors, not self-identification. Images are selected from MS-Celeb-1M (celebrity web images), so the population is public figures and the images are uncontrolled web photographs.

router.standardisation: robust: (x - median) / (IQR / 1.349), statistics over all images with landmarks

embedding: not used (Part B runs measurement 1 only; no embeddings computed)

provenance.source_dataset: RFW (Racial Faces in-the-Wild), test subsets only
provenance.derived_from: MS-Celeb-1M, withdrawn by its creator (Microsoft) in April 2019
provenance.access: granted in writing by Mei Wang (Beijing University of Posts and Telecommunications) on 2026-10-20, in response to a request from Applied Science Private University
provenance.obtained_from: the Google Drive link supplied by the maintainer, not a mirror
provenance.downloaded: the four test subsets only (Caucasian, Asian, Indian, African); the MS1M-wo-RFW and BUPT training sets distributed alongside them were not downloaded
provenance.verification: unpacked tree verified file by file against the official counts (40,607 images, 11,429 identities) before use; re-verified by faceshape_pilot.stage4.rfw on every run

keep_rule: landmark detection succeeded, and the identity still has >= 2 such images

notes: A failure is an image with no landmarks (decode failures included; none expected, counted separately).
groups.*: Wilson CIs and chi-square over images (from stage3.part_a.failure_by_group); these treat images as independent.

per_group.*_ci95_identity_bootstrap and highest_minus_lowest: identities resampled with replacement within each group, N_BOOTSTRAP=1000, seed stream [SEED, 42, group index]; this respects clustering of failures within identity.
highest/lowest are chosen by point estimate before bootstrapping, so the CI on their difference is conditional on that selection.

B1_pooled.description: one standardiser fitted on the ratio features of all four RFW groups pooled (primary)

notes: p_top1 is computed over unordered pairs; p_topk, per-class values and kappa over ordered pairs (both directions).
p_top1_given_probe_class equals the specific (positive) agreement for that class because both directions are counted.
mean_classes_searched is exactly k under fixed top-k multi-probe; mean_gallery_fraction_searched is the cost in images.
CIs: 95% percentile bootstrap over identities, pair sample held fixed.

Groups are resampled independently: identities with replacement within each group, N_BOOTSTRAP=1000, seed stream [SEED, 41, group index]; the pair sample is the one m1_consistency draws and is held fixed.
p_value_bootstrap = 2 * min(P*(d <= 0), P*(d >= 0)) with the +1 correction; it agrees with 'ci_excludes_zero' up to percentile discreteness.
Holm step-down across the six pairwise comparisons, alpha = 0.05, separately per metric and per condition. Only significant_holm supports a claim of a difference.

Spread: point = max group minus min group by point estimate. ci95_replicate_max_minus_min is the percentile CI of max_g - min_g over replicates (biased upward when groups are equal, so it never covers zero); ci95_fixed_pair_difference is the CI of the difference for the two groups named.
